entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 26 Is 26:1-21 . Connected with the Twenty-fourth and Twenty-fifth Chapters. Song of Praise of Israel after Being Restored to Their Own Land. As the overthrow of the apostate faction is described in the twenty-fifth chapter, so the peace of the faithful is here described under the image of a well-fortified city. 1. strong city-- Jerusalem, strong in Jehovah's protection: type of the new Jerusalem ( Psa 48:1-3 ), contrasted with the overthrow of the ungodly foe ( Is 26:4-7, 12 - 14 ; Re 22:2 , 10-12 , &c.). salvation ... walls-- ( Is 60:18 ; Jr 3:23 ; Zec 2:5 ). Maurer translates, "Jehovah makes His help serve as walls" ( Is 33:20 , 21 , &c.). bulwarks-- the trench with the antemural earthworks exterior to the wall.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8771"/><div sID="gen14564" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8771"/><hi type="bold">3. mind ... stayed--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Ps.112.7">Psa 112:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.112.8">8</reference>). Jesus can create "perfect peace" within thy mind, though storms of trial rage without (<reference osisRef="Isa.57.19">Is 57:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mark.4.39">Mr 4:39</reference>); as a city kept securely by a strong garrison within, though besieged without (so <reference osisRef="Phil.4.7">Php 4:7</reference>). "Keep," literally, "guard as with a garrison." Horsley translates, (God's) workmanship (the Hebrew does not probably mean "mind," but "a thing formed," <reference osisRef="Eph.2.10">Ep 2:10</reference>), so constantly "supported"; or else "formed and supported (by Thee) Thou shalt preserve (it, namely, the righteous nation) in perpetual peace." <div eID="gen14564" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 3. mind ... stayed-- ( Psa 112:7 , 8 ). entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8772"/><div sID="gen14565" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8772"/><hi type="bold">4. Lord Jehovah--</hi>Hebrew, Jah, Jehovah. The union of the two names expresses in the highest degree God's unchanging love and power (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.68.4">Psa 68:4</reference>). This passage, and <reference osisRef="Isa.12.2">Is 12:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Exod.6.3">Ex 6:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.83.18">Psa 83:18</reference>, are the four in which the English Version retains the Jehovah of the original. Maurer translates, "For Jah (the eternal unchangeable One, <reference osisRef="Exod.3.14">Ex 3:14</reference>) is Jehovah, the rock of ages" (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.45.17">Is 45:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.32.15">De 32:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Sam.2.2">1Sa 2:2</reference>). <div eID="gen14565" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 4. Lord Jehovah-- Hebrew, Jah, Jehovah. The union of the two names expresses in the highest degree God's unchanging love and power (compare Psa 68:4 ). This passage, and Is 12:2 ; Ex 6:3 ; Psa 83:18 , are the four in which the English Version retains the Jehovah of the original. Maurer translates, "For Jah (the eternal unchangeable One, Ex 3:14 ) is Jehovah, the rock of ages" (compare Is 45:17 ; De 32:15 ; 1Sa 2:2 ).

Rather, "wind" is a figure for that which proves an abortive effort. The "we" is in antithesis to "Thy," "my" (<reference osisRef="Isa.26.19">Is 26:19</reference>), what we vainly attempt, God will accomplish.<div eID="gen14593" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14594" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">not wrought ... deliverance in ... earth--</hi>literally, "the land (Judea) is not made security," that is, is not become a place of security from our enemies.<div eID="gen14594" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14595" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">neither ... world fallen--</hi>The "world" at large, is in antithesis to "the earth," that is, Judea. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8787"/><div sID="gen14596" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8787"/>19. In antithesis to <reference osisRef="Isa.26.14">Is 26:14</reference>, "They (Israel's foes) shall not live"; "Thy (Jehovah's) dead men (the Jews) shall live," that is, primarily, be restored, spiritually (<reference osisRef="Isa.54.1-Isa.54.3">Is 54:1-3</reference>), civilly and nationally (<reference osisRef="Isa.26.15">Is 26:15</reference>); whereas Thy foes shall not; ultimately, and in the fullest scope of the prophecy, restored to life literally (<reference osisRef="Ezek.37.1-Ezek.37.14">Eze 37:1-14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Dan.12.2">Da 12:2</reference>).<div eID="gen14596" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14597" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">together with my dead body--</hi>rather, "my dead body," or "bodies" (the Jewish nation personified, which had been spiritually and civilly dead; or the nation, as a parent, speaking of the bodies of her children individually, see on <reference osisRef="Isa.26.9">Is 26:9</reference>, "I," "My"): Jehovah's "dead" and "my dead" are one and the same [Horsley]. However, as Jesus is the antitype to Israel (<reference osisRef="Matt.2.15">Mt 2:15</reference>), English Version gives a true sense, and one ultimately contemplated in the prophecy: Christ's dead body being raised again is the source of Jehovah's people (all, and especially believers, the spiritual Israelites) also being raised (<reference osisRef="1Cor.15.20-1Cor.15.22">1Co 15:20-22</reference>).<div eID="gen14597" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14598" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Awake--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Eph.5.14">Ep 5:14</reference>), spiritually.<div eID="gen14598" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14599" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in dust--</hi>prostate and dead, spiritually and nationally; also literally (<reference osisRef="Isa.25.12">Is 25:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.47.1">47:1</reference>).<div eID="gen14599" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14600" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">dew--</hi>which falls copiously in the East and supplies somewhat the lack of rain (<reference osisRef="Hos.14.5">Ho 14:5</reference>).<div eID="gen14600" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14601" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">cast out ... dead--</hi>that is, shall bring them forth to life again. <div eID="gen14601" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 19. In antithesis to Is 26:14 , "They (Israel's foes) shall not live"; "Thy (Jehovah's) dead men (the Jews) shall live," that is, primarily, be restored, spiritually ( Is 54:1-3 ), civilly and nationally ( Is 26:15 ); whereas Thy foes shall not; ultimately, and in the fullest scope of the prophecy, restored to life literally ( Eze 37:1-14 ; Da 12:2 ). together with my dead body-- rather, "my dead body," or "bodies" (the Jewish nation personified, which had been spiritually and civilly dead; or the nation, as a parent, speaking of the bodies of her children individually, see on Is 26:9 , "I," "My"): Jehovah's "dead" and "my dead" are one and the same [Horsley]. However, as Jesus is the antitype to Israel ( Mt 2:15 ), English Version gives a true sense, and one ultimately contemplated in the prophecy: Christ's dead body being raised again is the source of Jehovah's people (all, and especially believers, the spiritual Israelites) also being raised ( 1Co 15:20-22 ). Awake-- ( Ep 5:14 ), spiritually. in dust-- prostate and dead, spiritually and nationally; also literally ( Is 25:12 ; 47:1 ). dew-- which falls copiously in the East and supplies somewhat the lack of rain ( Ho 14:5 ). cast out ... dead-- that is, shall bring them forth to life again.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8788"/><div sID="gen14602" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8788"/><hi type="bold">20. enter ... chambers--</hi>When God is about to take vengeance on the ungodly, the saints shall be shut in by Him in a place of safety, as Noah and his family were in the days of the flood (<reference osisRef="Gen.7.16">Ge 7:16</reference>), and as Israel was commanded not to go out of doors on the night of the slaying of the Egyptian first-born (<reference osisRef="Exod.12.22">Ex 12:22</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.12.23">23</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.31.20">Psa 31:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.83.3">83:3</reference>). The saints are calmly and confidently to await the issue (<reference osisRef="Exod.14.13">Ex 14:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.14.14">14</reference>). <div eID="gen14602" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 20. enter ... chambers-- When God is about to take vengeance on the ungodly, the saints shall be shut in by Him in a place of safety, as Noah and his family were in the days of the flood ( Ge 7:16 ), and as Israel was commanded not to go out of doors on the night of the slaying of the Egyptian first-born ( Ex 12:22 , 23 ; Psa 31:20 ; 83:3 ). The saints are calmly and confidently to await the issue ( Ex 14:13 , 14 ).

navigation_sections.content_plain: CHAPTER 26 Is 26:1-21 . Connected with the Twenty-fourth and Twenty-fifth Chapters. Song of Praise of Israel after Being Restored to Their Own Land. As the overthrow of the apostate faction is described in the twenty-fifth chapter, so the peace of the faithful is here described under the image of a well-fortified city.
